items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1972-06-16
items.q: I played with all of them. Joe Rochelle was on piano, though.

ctx.x: What? What did Martin play? Drums. Oh, you ever said drums?

Oh man, I can't remember. That had been so long. I played with all of them. Joe Rochelle was on piano, though. I remember that. All of them people was dead, not what I'm talking about. Yeah, he was dead. Who played band you? Who played band you? I think Sills. Sills. He named Sills. He played on the record? Yeah. He named Sills. He was some dude. Daniel Barker, one of them.

Didn't you tell me something about them having different drummers in that band, Lars? Did you change, did this fellow Martin play with the band all the time? Yeah. The drum player. Martin? Didn't you have different drum players in the band? You changed drums? My first band? No, in Lee Collins' band. Did they have the same drum player all the time?

items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: when he was playing with Joe Robichelper in Paradise

ctx.x: Yeah, don't forget about that. Leo used to call him the Paul Bones. See, Paul Bones played a better size boy, and Leo used to call him the geesh, I was Paul Bones.

Well, see, when he was playing with Joe Robichelper in Paradise, man, I used to go up there in here, man, and I used to be off, man. I used to go up there, spend my time up there, man. Water cat, water cat could play, boy. Poor boy had two strokes, man. Young boy, too. Very young, yeah. He was young, too.
Oh, what I wanted to ask you was, did you do any parade work? Any parade work?
